candidates.title: Sort incoming referral responses

demandEvidence.chore: Handle incoming referral responses and documents in a clerical workflow; no clinical review or real records.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: hantering av inkommande remissvar, post- och dokumenthantering

ease.reason: A fictional queue is mockable, but no attached reference supports referral-response sorting.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a clinic might value clerical time saved; the vacancy proves no AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: Synthetic labels can test routing drafts, but the notice gives no categories or routing rules.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable draft queue is conceivable; staff must classify, verify and route every item.

evidence.reason: The paid notice names incoming referral responses and document handling, not fields or software.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: assess only a fictional referral-response routing draft; the notice supplies no categories, and no attached reference supports the mechanics. Real records and all clinical judgment stay out of scope.

candidates.title: Make a fictional booking follow-up list

ease.reason: A mock list is accessible, but no attached reference supports booking workflows.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: clinics may value less clerical follow-up; this notice does not establish AI buyers.

feasibility.reason: Fictional entries can test sorting, but eligibility, urgency and booking rules are absent.

autonomy.reason: Sorting can repeat; a staff member must verify priority and make all bookings.

evidence.reason: The notice explicitly names waiting lists and bookings, but not inputs, cadence or tools.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the notice identifies waiting lists and bookings but supplies no sorting rules; no attached reference supports booking mechanics. A fictional list cannot make real patient priorities or bookings.
